title: Make a Pythagorean-theorem short
blurb: Animate the classic dissection proof of the Pythagorean theorem with the JS Shell and the Universal Timeline.
desc: Build three squares and a right triangle, animate the classic dissection proof, add a background, and end on a living call-card — all with the JS Shell and the Universal Timeline.

title: Build a night scene from scratch
blurb: The from-scratch workflow: helper functions, noise-displaced ground, night lighting, a moving object and a hero camera.
desc: Reusable helper functions, a noise-displaced ground, a grouped structure, night lighting (and the Environment setting that silently undoes it), a moving object, and a static hero camera — the full from-scratch workflow.

title: Add a static hero camera to a render sequence
blurb: Cut a fixed hero camera into a render sequence to show a moment your main camera does not frame well.
desc: A focused deep-dive on just the Render tab's Camera Sequence feature — add a fixed, non-animated camera and cut it in to showcase one moment your main animated camera doesn't frame well.

title: Build a table-view pong scene
blurb: Build Pong as a receding table, and verify the camera framing by projecting points to screen space.
desc: Build Pong as a real receding table instead of a flat arcade screen — pick the depth axis before placing anything, group parts with one AddObjectCommand, verify camera framing by projecting points to NDC, and swap the backdrop for a sunset desert without touching the table.

title: Build a bubble shooter scene
blurb: A lane, one class-tagged bubble template for game code to clone, a rainforest backdrop and a score sign.
desc: Build the scene, not the game: a lane, exactly one class-tagged Bubble template for runtime logic to clone and recolor, a rainforest background, and a wooden single-score sign — plus two real bugs (a local-space distance offset, and JavaScript's negative modulo) worth checking for.

title: Build a fighting-game arena scene
blurb: A tavern stage, two class-tagged fighters and a health-and-mana HUD, built for game code to drive.
desc: Build the scene, not the game: a plank-floor stage with a tavern backdrop, two class-tagged fighter placeholders facing each other, a health-and-mana HUD whose fills are anchored so game code only sets scale.x, and a round timer — plus the rotated-rig axis bug, and a ready-made fight.json to open.

title: Build a wizard hat and sculpt a face into it
blurb: Assemble a hat from primitives, then sculpt a relief smiley into it as one undoable step.
desc: Assemble a floppy purple hat from a lathe brim, a three-section bending cone, a band, a buckle and extruded stars, then sculpt a real relief smiley into it: a dense mesh pushed out along its normals using surface coordinates, as one undoable step — plus the z-fighting joint bug and the cylinder-seam normals trap.

title: Build a labelled racing circuit with a script
blurb: Generate a whole circuit from corner points and name every object at creation so game engines can find it.
desc: Generate a whole circuit from thirteen corner points: a road ribbon on rolling terrain, a harbour built from shared shapes, and every object named and classed at creation so a game engine can find the start line, checkpoints, grid and racing line. Check it, export it, read the GLB back, and play it in strata-play — plus the traps (a material named like a class, a sun that points the wrong way, 236 materials where ten were authored).

title: Make your own MetaHuman
blurb: Import a MetaHuman GLB, restyle it, pose its 51 face blendshapes and capture a still.
desc: Import a MetaHuman GLB straight from the metahuman-to-glb project's URL, then make it yours with the JS Shell: hide the hair, retint the skin and swap the outfit, pose the 51 ARKit face blendshapes, tag parts with classes, and capture a still with the Render tab's Take Snapshot.

title: One dance, two characters
blurb: Bake one Mixamo dance onto two different characters and stage them with an orbiting camera.
desc: Two different sources — a Mixamo FBX and a MetaHuman GLB — map natively into Strata through bodyrig-webCLI: download The Boss from Mixamo and Bruce from metahuman-to-glb, bake the same dance onto both, then stage them on a blank white stage: Bruce leads, The Boss copies three seconds later, and an orbiting camera keeps their faces in frame.

title: Restyle a VRM into an explorer with the JS Shell
blurb: Restyle a VRoid base model into an expedition explorer: retint, re-clothe, attach gear and pose a smirk.
desc: Download the free VRoid base model from 52blendshapes-for-VRoid-face, import the .vrm, and restyle it into a generic expedition explorer with the JS Shell: retint hair and skin, cut the clothes into a crop top and shorts, attach a belt, satchel and headband to the skeleton, lower the arms, and pose a smirk with the ARKit blendshapes.

title: A martial-arts lesson, then a sparring match, in a bamboo dojo
blurb: Two characters share one mocap clip in a bamboo dojo: a lesson, then a sparring match filmed by four cameras.
desc: Two rigged VRoid characters share one mocap clip: stage a teacher and a student face to face, have the student repeat the routine in chunks, then build a dojo floor, a bamboo hut with warm lantern lighting, and a four-camera render sequence — plus the two skinned-mesh pitfalls (parts vanishing, slow playback) that two characters expose, and a pass that dresses the characters, gives them a face (gaze, a seeded blink) and re-lights the hut. Part 2 swaps in two fighters from a two-person capture and turns the lesson into a 170-second sparring match, with cameras that follow the pair and shots cut by distance and verified frame by frame.

title: Editing captured motion as data
blurb: Cut a 170-second two-performer capture to 53 seconds with a non-destructive edit list.
desc: Cut a 170-second two-performer capture to 53 seconds with a non-destructive edit list: register the pair, splice eight spans with a blend, check hip-to-hip collisions, remap the cameras, then undo or clear it — all from the JS Shell, and the capture itself is never modified.

title: Authoring a face: gaze and idle
blurb: Give two characters a face with timeline keys: gaze that follows, a seeded blink and held expressions.
desc: Give two characters a face with timeline keys: named-target gaze that follows a moving character (eyes lead, head lags, anatomical clamp), a seeded blink / breath idle layer under the keys, and held expressions with easing and duration — authored from the JS Shell, mirrored in the Customize tab, deterministic, and no face capture.

title: A sparring match from a two-person motion capture
blurb: Turn a two-person sparring capture into a 53-second match, checked frame by frame for collisions.
desc: Turn a 170-second OptiTrack capture of two people sparring (recorded in the Martial Arts and Motion Capture course, GAME 294, ASU — run by Pavan Turaga, recorded by Assegid Kidane) into a 53-second match: register the pair, cut it with a non-destructive edit list, check every frame for collisions, move the camera shots onto the new timeline, and give both fighters an eyeline and an idle face — all from the JS Shell.

title: Strata Play tutorials
blurb: Run, fork and wire up games: the entry module, label-driven physics, and a racing circuit.
desc: Tutorials for Strata Play, the sandboxed player for the scenes you build here: play a game from a repo URL, write your first entry module, see how labels become physics, drive one logic across many scenes, add sound and settings, and wire up the labelled racing circuit from the Strata tutorial.
